correctness.rationale: In uniform G(n,m), conditioning on degree(v)=1 leaves an independent uniform (n-1)-vertex induced graph with m-1 edges; every non-induced motif H of minimum degree >=2 excludes v. Exact embedding counts and E[L]=n P(degree(v)=1) give Cov(L,X_H)=E[L]E[X_H]((n-h)/n*(m-e)/m*(N)_e/(A)_e-1), for e<=m<=A+1, zero otherwise. The normalized bracket is strictly increasing by K*e/[m(m+1)]. For H=triangle the continuous zero m*=3(n+1)(n²-n-4)/(3n²-3n-4) lies in (n,n+1) for each n>=5, giving negative sign m=3..n and positive m=n+1..A+1. From hypergeometric asymptotics, for fixed c>0, m=floor(cn) covariance tends to 8c³(c-1)exp(-2c). The n=4 exception, h>=3, n>=h+1 and finite support are handled. Independent direct enumeration of all 2^10 simple graphs on 5 vertices and 2^15 on 6 vertices matched exact covariance at every edge count (11 and 16 levels). The universal conclusion uses the conditioning proof, not finite tests.
